- Provide production IP ranges for allowlist (CIDR). If you have a specific egress NAT IP for the Redwood ingestion nodes, share that too.
- Confirm primary SCIM attribute mapping for 'email' and 'employeeNumber' — we included a default map in scim-attribute-map.md.
- Create a service account in your IAM for 'redwood-onboard' with the delegated SAML trust; list the owner contact.

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- 2026-09-22: Staging test (non-prod) — validate SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning + IP allowlist acceptance.
- 2026-09-28: Canary cutover (10% traffic) — observe auth logs and token success/failures.
- 2026-10-05: Full cutover.

Ben, Monica — looping you in for the implementation steps and to confirm the staging checklist. I put the MOP and IP template in Drive (link below).

Attachments: keystone-mop-v1.xlsx, ip-allowlist-template.csv, scim-attribute-map.md

Thanks,
Sean

Liam / Sean — short technical note to make the cutover as low-friction as possible. TL;DR: for staging you only need to allow SAML redirects to our control-plane domains and permit outbound HTTPS to our SCIM endpoints. No persistent inbound to your cluster is required. Details below: 

Steps for staging (non-prod):
1) SAML: add our assertion consumer endpoint https://auth.redwood.ai/saml/acs to your SP configuration; we will send a test assertion via the staging tenant.
2) IPs: allow outbound from your infra to the following control-plane ranges (these are TLS egress only): 35.230.11.0/24, 35.230.12.0/24. The ip-allowlist-template.csv has these filled in. If your egress NAT differs, we will record your NAT IP in our allowlist.
3) SCIM: provide a service account token and the base SCIM URL (e.g., https://scim.keystonefin.com) — we will do a dry-run provisioning against a staging org. Refer to scim-attribute-map.md for the mapping we will use. Typical mapping we prefer: email -> userPrincipalName, employeeNumber -> employee_id, displayName -> name.
4) Service account roles: we only require a scoped token for SCIM create/read/update; do not grant wide admin rights. The minimum permissions we need are User:Create, User:Read, Group:Read.
5) Audit: during staging we will deliver an audit bundle (logs + token events) to your security team after the run.

Fallback plan: if SCIM provisioning errors spike beyond 5% during the canary, we will rollback SCIM writes and switch to manual provisioning for the remainder of the test window.

Attached: ip-allowlist-template.csv (populated), quick-scim-sample-requests.txt (in Drive), keystone-mop-v1.xlsx (staging tab completed).

Ben Carter
Technical Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
